messages:
amy: Heads-up — onboarding Pomelo24b-int4 looks good functionally but we're hitting OOMs on canary with long generations (~>300 tokens) when batch_size >= 4.

carlos: +1 saw p99 spikes and OOMs on a few instances. repro command I ran: `rctl run --model pomelo24b-int4 --batch 4 --max_new_tokens 512 --seq 2048 --prompt tests/long_prompt.json` => JVM / python process killed.

tilly: logs from the node: `cuda out of memory` but also a lot of memory fragmentation markers in the runtime log. copying snippet: `MEM_FRAG WARNING: slots_free 128, largest_free 24MB, total_free 512MB`

amy: Interesting — fragmentation rather than raw lack. Are we seeing KV cache blowup? what's the session cache size?

carlos: session cache default=8 sessions. When requests include long context + long gen we allocate 2x KV per request due to prefetching pattern. That plus int4 alignment padding seems to push allocation into fragmented space.

sahil: Quick mitigation: reduce default max_new_tokens for Pomelo to 256 and lower default batch size to 2. That buys headroom. Also try enabling slot_compaction on the node: `infractl patch node --enable-slot-compaction=true`

amy: Can we do a softer change first? e.g., model config override: `defaults: { max_new_tokens: 256, batch_window_ms: 40, max_batch_size: 2 }` and add a rollout with canary 10%?

tilly: I pushed a canary with those defaults to a small pool. So far no OOMs for the last 45m but p99 latency increased ~6%.

carlos: Perf tradeoff expected. Also saw that prefetch=aggressive triggers prefetch of both KV and weights. Try switching to `prefetch: conservative` for pomelo24b-int4 to limit early allocations.

sahil: Another operational tweak: set `kv_prune_threshold=0.6` and `kv_eviction_policy=LRU-age` — this prunes old KV entries sooner which helps fragmentation when many long sessions are idle.

amy: Good. For a longer term fix we should look at quantized packing alignment — int4 uses nibble packing leading to weird free-list fragmentation. Engineering ticket?

carlos: I'll open one. Notes: reproducer script in repo at `eng-ml/bench/repro_pomelo_oom.sh`. Attach logs + sample prompts. Proposal: 1) short-term defaults change + prefetch conservative + kv_prune; 2) node-level slot_compaction toggle; 3) runtime allocator change to coalesce small free blocks (follow-up PR).

tilly: Also let's enable automatic fallback: if request would exceed estimated working set (estimator currently off), route to pomelo24b-int8 variant or to dedicated pool with reserved slots. Fallback patch I sketched: `router: if est_wset > node_free * 0.8 -> fallback to pomelo24b-int8`

amy: +1 on fallback. Can we also add an alert to slack when a node returns 3 OOMs in 5m so SRE can bail out?

infra-bot: alert created: #inc-oom-pomelo (threshold 3 OOMs / 5m).

sahil: TL;DR action list: (1) deploy model config defaults change (max_new_tokens=256, max_batch_size=2, batch_window_ms=40) to 10% canary now, (2) patch prefetch to conservative for canary, (3) infra: enable slot_compaction on canary nodes, (4) open eng ticket for allocator coalescing and int4 packing audit, (5) add router fallback rule, (6) add OOM alert to #inc-oom-pomelo.

amy: I'll own the config rollout and monitor. Carlos please open the allocator ticket with repro attached. Tilly, update the canary notes in the model onboarding doc.

carlos: On it. created ticket ENG-ML-1429 with steps and logs.

tilly: Can we collect a small eval to compare quality delta when falling back to int8? I'll run eval set A/B over night and post numbers tomorrow.

amy: Perfect. Keep posts short in this thread; if we see OOMs after canary -> escalate to release-war-room. :thumbsup:
